citation: FIPAT. Terminologia Anatomica. 2nd ed. Federative International Programme for Anatomical Terminology, 2019.
variables_provided: Canonical names; formal heads/parts; synonyms; term numbers
limitations: Terminology establishes named anatomy, not whether a subdivision should receive an independently inferable training state.

citation: Riem L, Pinette M, DuCharme O, et al. Big bones mean big muscles: an MRI-based dataset of muscle-bone-body size relationships across 70 human muscles of the upper limb, trunk, and lower limb. J Appl Physiol. 2026;140:1-19.
population: Active healthy adults; male subset used for reference morphology
age: 18-50 y; male summary in report ~32 ± 10 y
measurement_method: Whole-body 3-T Dixon MRI; AI-assisted segmentation with manual review
coverage: 70 muscles/source ROIs + 13 bones across upper limb, trunk, lower limb
variables_provided: Muscle volume; volume fraction; fat fraction; asymmetry; muscle-bone/body-size relationships
limitations: Several source ROIs are composites; not all canonical muscles/segments are individually resolved; architecture not provided.

citation: Charles JP, Suntaxi F, Anderst WJ. In vivo human lower limb muscle architecture dataset obtained using diffusion tensor imaging. PLoS ONE. 2019;14(10):e0223531.
measurement_method: 3-T MRI + DTI fibre tractography; anatomical position
variables_provided: Muscle volume; muscle length; optimal fibre length; pennation; PCSA; modelled Fmax
limitations: Mixed-sex small cohort. Optimal fibre lengths use sarcomere lengths from Ward et al.; PCSA therefore published-derived rather than wholly direct. Not eligible as adult-male canonical mean.

citation: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL. Are current measurements of lower extremity muscle architecture accurate? Clin Orthop Relat Res. 2009;467(4):1074-1082.
measurement_method: Cadaver dissection; fibre bundles; sarcomere-normalised fibre length; pennation; PCSA
variables_provided: Muscle mass; muscle length; fibre length; sarcomere length; pennation; PCSA
limitations: Broad, internally coherent architecture dataset but elderly mixed-sex cadavers. Strong for structural relationships and segment-specific hamstring/gastrocnemius architecture; not an adult-male population prior.

citation: Stiver ML, et al. Three-dimensional muscle architecture of the infant and adult trapezius: a cadaveric pilot study. Anatomy. 2021;15(1):26-35.
population: Adult pilot specimen plus infant comparison
variables_provided: Fibre-bundle length; muscle volume; PCSA; segment proportions
limitations: Only one adult specimen. Useful for the existence and order-of-magnitude of part-specific architecture and proportional PCSA; must remain high-uncertainty.

citation: Fung L, Wong B, Ravichandiran K, Agur A, Rindlisbacher T, Elmaraghy A. Three-dimensional study of pectoralis major muscle and tendon architecture. Clin Anat. 2009;22(4):500-508.
coverage: Pectoralis major clavicular and sternal architecture; sternal subdivisions
variables_provided: Fibre-bundle length; pennation; 3-D fibre orientation; tendon architecture
limitations: Resolves clavicular versus sternal architecture better than My Mettle's three-part clavicular/sternocostal/abdominal scheme. Do not manufacture an abdominal-part PCSA or volume split from this source.

citation: Murray WM, Buchanan TS, Delp SL. The isometric functional capacity of muscles that cross the elbow. J Biomech. 2000;33(8):943-952.
measurement_method: Cadaveric architectural dissection with sarcomere normalisation
coverage: Major elbow flexors/extensors and selected forearm muscles
variables_provided: Optimal fibre length; PCSA; functional capacity
limitations: Useful elbow-region architecture but incomplete for My Mettle's three triceps heads; should not be treated as a young-adult-male reference.

citation: Architectural properties of neuromuscular compartments in selected forearm skeletal muscles. 2014.
coverage: FCR; FCU; ECRB; ECU; pronator teres compartments
variables_provided: Fascicle length; pennation; PCSA by compartment
limitations: Excellent demonstration that named/neuromuscular subdivisions can have distinct architecture. My Mettle currently keeps these as SHARED_PARENT, so the values inform recruitment/mechanics rather than separate development states.

citation: Architecture of rectus abdominis, quadratus lumborum, and erector spinae. 2001.
coverage: Rectus abdominis; quadratus lumborum; erector-spinae components
limitations: Small older-cadaver study. Useful where modern in-vivo architecture is unavailable; do not present as young-male canonical physiology.

citation: Architectural analysis and predicted functional capability of human latissimus dorsi. 2013.
coverage: Latissimus dorsi whole muscle and regional origins
variables_provided: Fascicle length; PCSA; regional PCSA/volume contribution
limitations: Shows genuine regional architecture but does not justify creating upper/lower latissimus development segments in v1.

citation: Unique morphological architecture of the hamstring muscles. J Anat. 2023.
coverage: Semimembranosus; semitendinosus; biceps femoris long and short heads
variables_provided: PCSA; pennation; fibre-to-muscle-length ratio; sarcomere length
limitations: Directly resolves biceps-femoris heads and is therefore highly relevant structurally; demographic compatibility remains poor for an adult-male reference.

citation: Flack NAMS, Nicholson HD, Woodley SJ. The anatomy of the hip abductor muscles. Clin Anat. 2014.
coverage: Gluteus medius and gluteus minimus compartments
limitations: Supports compartmental organisation but identifies a more complex four-compartment pattern rather than My Mettle's deliberately coarse anterior/middle/posterior fibre regions. Do not force a 1:1 numerical mapping.

citation: Changes in triceps surae muscle architecture with sarcopenia. 2005.
variables_provided: Muscle volume; fascicle length; pennation; PCSA
limitations: Highly compatible population for gastrocnemius-head priors. Numerical table still requires durable extraction before canonical selection.

citation: Peterson SL, Rayan GM. Shoulder and upper arm muscle architecture. J Hand Surg Am. 2011.
coverage: 11 shoulder and upper-arm muscles including deltoid/biceps/triceps
variables_provided: Fibre length; pennation; PCSA; architectural classification
limitations: Small elderly sample; useful for relative head/part architecture but not adult-male morphology. Exact segment-value extraction still required.

citation: In vivo diffusion-tensor architectural study of adductor magnus portions. 2025.
measurement_method: In-vivo MRI/DTI with fascicle-insertion based partitioning
limitations: Modern in-vivo evidence but its three-part partition is not equivalent to My Mettle's adductor-versus-hamstring two-part ontology. Keep mapping incompatible until an explicit crosswalk is justified.
